criteria.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-core` passes including a new slots test where two jobs need local checks with max_check_slots = 1: the second waits while the first holds the slot, then runs after release (asserted by order and a nonzero queued_s for the second).
criteria.evidence: In run/tests.rs, `two_jobs_with_one_build_slot_run_one_after_the_other` runs two `Athena::go` calls on threads at the default of one slot. The first fake check waits until `SlotQueue::waiting() >= 1`, and the second asserts `inside == 0`. The test asserts the log is [first-start, first-end, second], and that the recorded `queued_s` values satisfy `waits[1] > 0 && waits[1] > waits[0]`. slots.rs `the_second_request_waits_then_runs` shows the same order at unit level. Both pass in the recorded CI `cargo test --locked` for f8da8d6. My own `cargo test -p athena-core slots::` failed to compile, but only because of an outdated athena-data build in the shared target dir: the source has `queued_s` at records.rs:823 and git status is clean.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test -p athena-core` includes a test where a slot holder's process dies (a child process holding the slot lock is killed, or a holder is dropped on panic/error) and a waiter then acquires the slot with no manual cleanup or sweeper.
criteria.evidence: slots.rs `a_killed_holder_frees_its_slot` starts the test binary again as a child that takes the only slot. With the child alive, `try_acquire` is refused. The test then sends SIGKILL with `child.kill()`, waits for the child, checks that the directory listing is unchanged (nothing was cleaned up), and a blocking `acquire` succeeds. `a_panicking_holder_frees_its_slot` and `a_holder_that_returns_an_error_frees_its_slot` cover a panic and an error return. All pass in the recorded CI run.

criteria.criterion: A test with max_check_slots = 2 shows at most 2 holders at once and a third request waits.
criteria.evidence: slots.rs `two_slots_admit_two_holders_and_the_third_waits` starts three threads that acquire on a queue of two slots. A shared counter tracks live holders, and the test asserts the peak is exactly 2, that `waiting() >= 1` while two are held, and that `try_acquire` is refused with two held. Athena's own fails-without run of this test failed (exit 101) on the reverted tree. Passes in CI.

criteria.criterion: A test shows a check request waiting past build_wait_s returns a resumable hold with reason `environment: build slot wait`, uses no attempt, and is not recorded as a work failure.
criteria.evidence: run/tests.rs `a_check_that_waits_past_build_wait_s_holds_the_job` sets `build_wait_s = 1` and holds the only slot. Checked in order: `go` returns a `SlotWait` error, and the output has a line starting `held       environment: build slot wait`. The job stays Dispatched with no outcome, no score and no verification, and no introspection is recorded. The verifier never ran (count 0). The resume mark is at the Checks stage. A second `go` names the build-slot wait, not 'was interrupted', and status shows the hold. After the holder is released, retry then go lands the job with no second producer run. The CLI drain test `a_build_slot_wait_holds_the_item_and_is_not_labelled_low_disk` asserts the item's outcome is `environment: build slot wait`, that it was attempted once, that no environment stop occurs and that there is no retry advice, then lands the job on the next pass. Passes in CI.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/slots.rs exists and SnapExec::exec in crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs acquires a guard from it before run_check and drops it after the snapshot restore, on every return path (guard released by Drop).
criteria.evidence: slots.rs exists (718 lines). In run/checks.rs lines 48-78, `let slot = self.slots.acquire(Class::Check, ..)?` comes before the seam and `run_check` call. `slot` stays in scope past `restore_to(self.prepared)?` and is read at line 77 for `queued_s`, so every early `?` return or panic drops it. `Slot` owns the locked `File`, whose Drop releases the flock. findings.summary: Files changed outside the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: These files are not on the expected deliverables list. All were in the planned files, and each change is needed. Most only add the `queued_s: None` literal that the compiler requires. close.rs adds the shared `commit_hold` and `hold_for_slot_wait`, which criterion 4 needs. drain.rs labels the outcome `environment: build slot wait` so the design's count of low-disk outcomes stays accurate. No unrelated behavior was added.

findings.summary: Fails-without reruns and baseline runs do not take a build slot yet, so concurrent cargo builds can still exceed max_check_slots
findings.evidence: Design section 4 lists 'local checks and reruns' under SnapExec::exec. The reruns and the baseline call `run_check` directly and bypass the slot. The added design note says so ('The baseline run and the "fails without" reruns are not wrapped yet'), and the request and criteria name only local checks, so this is a known gap for a later step, not a criterion miss.

findings.summary: Generic fallback wording for a held item replaced the low-disk default text
findings.evidence: `last_reason(&item.job, "free disk space is below the minimum")` became `"it was held and a later pass runs it"`. This is reasonable now that holds have more than one cause, but a low-disk hold that recorded no reason now shows less specific text. CI passes.

findings.summary: Slot-wait hold marker shares the low-disk marker file and is told apart by JSON shape
findings.evidence: Each reader tries its own struct shape on the same file. This works and is tested (`a_slot_wait_marker_shares_the_file_and_each_reader_reads_only_its_own_kind`), but a tagged enum would be clearer and more robust if a third kind of hold is added.

The likely cause is the earlier fails-without scratch builds. `cargo --config` was denied by policy, so I did not work around it. These criteria rely on the recorded CI `cargo test --locked` pass for this exact commit.

summary: The change does what the request and design section 8 step 3 ask. A new slots.rs builds a counting semaphore from `max_check_slots` lock files under `<state>/slots`. Waiters queue as locked ticket files ordered by class, then first come first served, with ageing. `SnapExec::exec` takes a slot after the first disk gate and holds it until after the snapshot restore. The slot is a `let` binding holding a `File`, so it is released on every return path, on a panic and when the process dies. A check that had to wait reads free disk space again before it runs. A wait past `build_wait_s` becomes a resumable `environment: build slot wait` hold. It uses no attempt, records no outcome, creates no introspection, and the drain reports it as its own outcome rather than as low disk. Config gains `build_wait_s` (default 1800) and `build_age_promote_s` (default 600), both validated as at least 1, and unknown keys are still refused. Each `CheckRun` gains an optional `queued_s`, and the status throughput section gains a 'build wait' line. The CHANGELOG and the design doc are updated, and athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows and records/ are untouched. I read the whole diff and design sections 4 and 8. I ran `cargo test -p athena-data records::` (73 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-data config::` (39 passed). I could not run the athena-core or athena-cli tests here: the shared build directory holds an outdated athena-data library that cargo treats as current, so athena-core fails to compile with 'no field queued_s', although the source has the field and git status is clean. The policy denied `cargo --config`, and I did not work around that. The behavior criteria therefore rest on the recorded CI `cargo test --locked` pass for exactly this commit (f8da8d6), which runs all the new tests; none is `#[ignore]`d. I also read each test and confirmed it would fail without the behavior. Remaining findings are minor: files outside the expected deliverables list, all planned and required; reruns and baseline runs not yet taking a slot, which the doc states openly; and one generic fallback wording change in the drain.
